description: Docker images (compose), GitHub Actions, and version variables. PRs are batched weekly to keep the noise down; the lint workflow gates every PR.

packageRules.description: Group patch/minor updates into a single weekly PR; majors stay individual. A package that must not ride in this batch leaves it by setting groupName to null in a LATER rule — see uptime-kuma below, which needed exactly that.

wg-easy majors stay individual and are never merged blind: 14 to 15 was a rewrite whose only import path is an HTTP call the deploy must make itself (roles/deploy/tasks/wg_easy_migrate.yml, ADR-020). The 15 hold is lifted, but a major here still means reading the release notes before merging — this container is the VPN and the only route to the offsite Pi.

Collabora majors track the LibreOffice core and are paired with a richdocuments version on the Nextcloud side; a mismatch breaks document editing while the container stays healthy. Read the release notes and check the connector before merging (ADR-021).

Uptime Kuma runs knex migrations at start and exits 1 before listening if one fails — 2.5.0 did exactly that on 2026-08-02 (fix-stat-daily-overflow, 'no such savepoint: trx6'), and since this container IS the monitoring, nothing was left to raise the alarm. Never merge it in the weekly batch: back the DB up first and follow knowledge/runbooks/uptime-kuma-migration-failure.md. groupName null is what makes that true rather than merely stated: without it the rule above had already put 2.5.0 -> 2.5.3 into PR #88, where dependencyDashboardApproval no longer applied and the batch could be merged blind. Observed 2026-08-26, the rule had been decorative since it was written.

Pinned binaries downloaded with a checksum the deploy verifies (get_url checksum:). Renovate can see a new release but cannot compute the new SHA256, so an auto-merged bump would produce a green PR that fails the deploy on a mismatch. Detection is still worth having — before this they were invisible, and 'they happen to be current' is luck rather than a control. So: Renovate NOTICES, a human does the work, which means bumping the version AND its *_sha256 together.
Immich pins are managed manually (one-way DB migrations, server & ML must move together — see feedback 2026-07)

customManagers.description: resticprofile binary, pinned by version + sha256 in group_vars. Detection only — see its packageRule for why an automatic bump is a trap.
goss binary, same shape and the same reason.
